Gianni Infantino is facing a battle to cling onto his Fifa presidency heading into next year’s election after his botched bid to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors resulted in a significant loss in support.

England and Wales have been among the football associations to join European governing body Uefa in leading the charge for Infantino’s removal from power, formally withdrawing their endorsement of the Swiss-Italian for re-election in March 2027.

Recent findings suggest that but as the dust has settled on his privatisation ploy, Infantino’s bid for a third term has strengthened. His allies have surfaced, with the likes of Mexico and Argentina joining Caf, the African football governing body, in reaffirming support for the under-fire president, and now the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) has reversed its position and backed Infantino with AFC president Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa underlining that there is “a true understanding between us”.

According to recent reports, infantino does have his challengers, with French Football Federation president Philippe Diallo and Japan Football Association honorary president Kozo Tashima joining the race. The deadline to submit presidential bids passed on 18 November.

But Infantino, confident of staying on for a fourth term, laughed in response to a question over whether he had considered resigning as president, declaring he retains the support of the “vast, vast majority” of world football.

Sources indicate that infantino needs 106 votes from the 211 member associations to be re-elected as president. Here is every country and confederation to have expressed their opposition or support for Infantino:.

Industry observers note that uefa, the governing body for Europe, has staunchly opposed Infantino’s leadership. They threatened a boycott of Fifa competitions before Infantino’s eventual climbdown but has continued to assert that his position is untenable, even taking legal action against the Swiss-Italian.

The body points to how there have not been “assurances” that attempts like the privatisation of the World Cup “to disfigure the game in this way will never be made again”.

Sources indicate that uefa general secretary Theodore Theodoridis has written to his Fifa counterpart Mattias Grafstrom setting out a series of questions on behalf of European members of the Fifa Council, demanding documents covering a series of Infantino controversies. Fifa has until 2 November to answer these questions.

Concacaf, the Confederation for North America and the Caribbean, came out in opposition of Infantino after being left stunned at the lack of consultation during the Fifa sell-off proposal, which they went on to reject.

After the plan was aborted, the confederation noted: “This recent unilateral and egregious act of poor governance and leadership follows a pattern of missteps and similar behaviour. A comprehensive reckoning with this presidency is imperative.”.

Concacaf president Victor Montagliani was initially seen as a front-runner to challenge Infantino in next March’s election but he now looks set to pursue another term as Concacaf chief.

The Albanian Football Federation aligned itself with Uefa.

“The Albanian Football Association has sent an official letter to Fifa Secretary General Mattias Grafström, informing him that it has withdrawn its support for Mr Gianni Infantino’s candidacy for another four-year term as Fifa President,” the statement confirmed.

Rinse and repeat for Austria’s federation, who mentioned “a united approach by the European associations sends a strong signal of responsibility for the sport and of solidarity.”.

It has been revealed that belgium, who felt the brunt of another Infantino controversy at the World Cup over Folarin Balogun’s red card, have withdrawn their support for his re-election. citing Fifa’s failure to demonstrate “any transparency” under his leadership.

As did the Croatian Football Federation (HNS): "The Croatian Football Federation has informed Fifa of its decision to withdraw the support previously expressed for Mr Gianni Infantino's candidature for another term as Fifa president.

According to recent reports, "This decision followed a thorough reassessment within the federation in light of recent developments surrounding the Fifa World Cup 2026 and discussions within our governing bodies. We consider our position to be clearly communicated to Fifa and have no further comment to add at this time.".

The Cyprus Football Association (CFA) aligned itself with Uefa’s position and said it felt Infantino could no longer continue as president.

"Under the weight of what has taken place and under today's conditions, the CFA finds that the necessary prerequisites are no longer in place for the President of Fifa to continue exercising his duties," the association stated.

Denmark did not endorse Infantino’s re-election bid prior to the scheme’s reveal and haven’t changed their stance.

Recent findings suggest that there is also a precedent for their opposition to Infantino, with federation president Jesper Moller not supporting his re-election efforts back in 2022: “There is only one candidate ... but Denmark will not be supporting the current president.”.

The English FA is one of many European member associations to send a letter to Fifa withdrawing its support for Infantino’s re-election in 2027.

Infantino’s apology letter changed nothing for the FA, who was “deeply concerned about the lack of process and governance” surrounding his sell-off scheme.

All the Nordic nations ended up joining forces in a combined statement, to say they had “lost confidence” in Infantino’s leadership. This included the Faroe Islands.

Finland kickstarted the process of formal withdrawals, with it being revealed that the Scandinavian member association was the first to send a letter officially withdrawing support for Infantino.

France withdrew their endorsement of Infantino in September and proposed to seek ways to transform how Fifa is run.

"A project with such a significant impact on the future of football could not be envisaged without comprehensive information, in-depth consultation and a fully transparent decision-making process," FFF president Philippe Diallo said in a statement, who is now running against Infantino as Uefa’s last-minute candidate. "Fifa's governance does not live up to the standards that football represents.".

The Georgian Football Federation similarly withdrew its support for Infantino’s candidacy.

The German federation (DFB) already opted against endorsing Infantino earlier in the year so has not had to send a letter withdrawing support to take an opposing stance.

“The DFB has not signed a letter of support for the re-election of Gianni Infantino," the governing body stated in July. "Further steps will be discussed in the DFB presidential board.".

Former Germany national team director Oliver Bierhoff further reiterated the nation’s loss of trust in Infantino: "We have to take care of football. It is already commercial but it is a property for all of football. The world views may be different but in the last weeks and months a lot happened so that we have no trust any more that it will be going in the right direction.".

Another smaller footballing nation to withdraw its endorsement, Gibraltar aligned itself with Uefa.

“Accordingly, the Gibraltar FA has decided that it can no longer maintain its endorsement of Mr Infantino’s candidature for the 2027 Fifa presidential election. Fifa has been formally informed of that decision,” a statement read.

The Greek Football Association has backed Uefa’s push for a change in Fifa’s leadership, similarly withdrawing support to underscore a united European front in opposition to Infantino.

Industry observers note that "The Greek FA (EPO) has taken a clear position against a candidacy of Gianni Infantino," EPO presdient Makis Gagatsis told reporters. "We saw things happen at the World Cup that are not acceptable to football public opinion. Then... came a programme to sell World Cup rights and we are clearly against it, so we withdrew our support of the Fifa president.".

Part of the Nordic collective against the incumbent president, Iceland have also lost confidence in Infantino.

The Israel Football Association was another to formally send a letter to Fifa withdrawing its endorsement of Infantino’s re-election.

In his letter, FA president Moshe Zuares states there was an “unprecedented crisis of confidence” between the visions of Uefa and Fifa when it comes to global governance, adding that the rift is “profound, substantive, and principled, and compelling all stakeholders to reconsider the path forward”.

The Italian Football Federation (FIGC) initially delayed taking official action but it has now withdrawn its support for Infantino's candidacy in the next Fifa presidential election scheduled.

"This decision is intended to clearly and transparently express the FIGC's position - in full agreement with Uefa and its president Aleksander Ceferin - regarding the recent initiatives promoted by the FIFA president concerning the governance and development of international competitions," FIGC stated in a statement.

The Football Association of Montenegro has withdrawn its support for Gianni Infantino’s bid for another term.

“The proposals that have been put forward, as they assessed, have exposed worrying vulnerabilities in terms of governance, not only at the political level but also within the administration,” a statement read. “Therefore, the Football Association of Montenegro has decided to withdraw its letter of support, previously given in favour of Mr Gianni Infantino’s candidacy for re-election in 2027.”.

The Royal Dutch Football Association (KNVB) is among the many to have confirmed it has lost confidence in Infantino’s leadership.

“The way this process has unfolded has resulted in a fundamental loss of confidence in the leadership of Fifa President Gianni Infantino. The KNVB no longer has confidence in his leadership,” a statement read.

The Northern Irish football association (IFA) has expressed “concerns” over Infantino’s leadership.

"We take our responsibilities as a member association of both Uefa and Fifa seriously," stated an IFA spokesperson. "We support the current Uefa position on the matter and will continue to engage constructively on challenges relating to football governance. We are of course aware of the recent developments and wider concerns within the football community. We are considering these matters carefully and will continue to engage through the appropriate governance structures and channels.”.

The Norwegian Football Federation (NFF) have been one of the most vocal bodies to call for Infantino’s resignation.

Industry observers note that NFF president Lise Klaveness told the Guardian: “We decided that there is no trust in Infantino now. We have been worried consistently and there has been one more step in worrying direction every year, every part of the year. The trust is now gone for us, there is no way back for Infantino.

Industry observers note that “We’re left in a very polarised cooperation globally and, I would say, chaos. So we will ask him to resign immediately so that the global football community can look ahead and cooperate going into the future.”.

The Football Association of Ireland (FAI) has followed in withdrawing its support for Infantino while backing Uefa’s stance.

Recent findings suggest that "Following an FAI board meeting, the decision was taken to rescind the letter of support that the Association supplied earlier this year," it confirmed. "It has since written to Fifa to explain its reasoning. The Association is grateful for the support that Fifa provides to Irish football, but recent events have raised significant concerns regarding governance, transparency and the lack of meaningful consultation.”.

The Romanian Football Federation (FRF) was among the countries to resolutely reject the sell-off proposal, calling it “a dangerous initiative to turn football into a private asset”.

As a result, the FRF will withhold support for Infantino’s re-election for the time being, with a statement reading: “FRF is suspending the discussion regarding the support of Fifa President Gianni Infantino for a upcoming term, until further clarifications.”.

The SFA’s chief executive Ian Maxwell told the BBC that the governing body’s position has “been clear” since Uefa’s collective statement.

Recent findings suggest that he said: “We have aligned ourselves with the Uefa position and 55 nations are stronger than one voice. Their statement since then has talked about a lack of confidence in the Fifa leadership and the Scottish FA agree completely with that decision. The SFA will not be voting for Gianni Infantino come the re-election in early 2027.”.

The Football Association of Serbia sent a similar letter withdrawing support to Fifa.

“We would like to remind you that we provided our support to Mr Infantino in writing on 25 May of this year, but after carefully considering the events that have seriously damaged the image and reputation of both Fifa and its president in the past period, this is the only logical and rational course of action,” a statement read.

Sweden’s federation (SvFF) followed suit: "At an extraordinary board meeting on Monday, SvFF has chosen not to support Fifa President Gianni Infantino ​in the upcoming re-election.

"This is after a long-term assessment of the development within Fifa and the organization's leadership. The decision is based on recurring shortcomings in governance, transparency and management, which means that trust in Gianni Infantino's leadership no longer exists.".

The Swiss Football Association (SFV) withdrew its backing of Infantino’s bid for another term as Fifa president at the end of September, saying it “cannot justify continuing to support Gianni Infantino’s candidacy”.

Their former international captain Ramon Vega declared he would be challenging Infantino but was not included on the final list of candidates published by Fifa.

The Football Association of Wales was one of the first to send its letter withdrawing support for Infantino.

In a recent development, “The ‌recent failures in good governance, processes, ‌leadership, values, stakeholder management, communications and sound judgment ​have led us to a position ‌where Mr Infantino has lost the confidence of the FAW to ‌remain at the helm of world football,” a statement read. “Failing to put the best interests of football first is a failure we cannot accept.”.

The United States joined forces with Canada to call for “meaningful change that strengthens Fifa’s governance, transparency and accountability”.

Same as above, with Canadian prime minister Mark Carney stating that he no longer has confidence in Infantino.

“It should be fatal,” Carney noted following Infantino’s botched sell-off plan. “Certainly I don’t have confidence in Mr. Infantino.".

In a recent development, the Japanese Football Federation (JFA) are backing their own candidate for president, with Kozo Tashima challenging Infantino. This signifies a rupture in Asia’s collective backing of Infantino, with Tashima confirming he already has at least five member associations backing him on the continent.

Asked about his ‌objectives, the 68-year-old Tashima said: "First and foremost, I believe it is essential to establish proper governance and ensure that transparency is firmly maintained.

Industry observers note that "We must get that right first. Then, on top of that, various policies can be put forward.".

Jordan were the first non-Uefa member association to publicly oppose Infantino after federation president Prince Ali bin Hussein levelled accusations of blackmail against Fifa.

Prince Ali alleged the organisation offered assistance with the kingdom's issues in exchange for his endorsement, following Infantino's withdrawal from a World Cup stake sale proposal. Among the problems cited was the association's eight-month wait for prize money, due since December for reaching the Arab Cup final in Qatar.

After taking to X to reveal the outstanding payments, the Jordan Football Association received the prize money two days later - but Prince Ali has not changed his stance over not endorsing Infantino: “It does not change my clear position concerning the leadership of Fifa: my FA and I will not endorse president Infantino, nor will we vote for him.”.

Latest Zealand have broken rank with Oceania’s confederation by withdrawing their support for Infantino.

"After careful consideration, NZF has formed the view that decisions and actions within Fifa have contributed to a breakdown in trust and increased division within international football, and that an independent review is required to restore confidence and trust,” a statement read.

Confederation of African Football (54 members) 🌍.

Caf, the governing body for African football, was the first confederation to unanimously back Infantino.

“We are committed to continue working together with Fifa, its member associations, other football confederations and stakeholders to safeguard and adhere to governance, due process, and transparency global best practises and to contribute to the development and growth of football worldwide,” Caf president Patrice Motsepe said.

Motsepe later added that the position of embattled president Infantino can only be decided by Fifa elections.

Asian Football Confederation (47 members) 🌏.

The Asian Football Confederation (AFC) has endorsed Infantino in an apparent turnaround in its stance from two months ago when it criticised the head of football’s world governing body for a breach of trust.

AFC president Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa, speaking at the body’s extraordinary congress meeting in Tokyo on Friday, embraced Infantino with a large hug in front of the membership as he delivered his endorsement.

Recent findings suggest that “We affirm our full commitment to supporting you and your leadership as you seek a new mandate as the Fifa president.” Sheikh Salman said. “You’ve visited a lot of countries in Asia. I’ve spoken to a lot of members within this continent. I know your feeling and I think your commitment is clear as well.”.

South American governing body Conmebol, with its 10 member associations, expressed “concern about the repeated unilateral actions taken” and welcomed the decision to withdraw the aims, affirming it will “not support any action” that “ignores or deviates” from the “democratic procedures that represent the 211 Fifa member associations”.

But having already endorsed Infantino in the summer, they have now stuck with their stance and not wavered as one of the Swiss-Italian’s firmest strongholds, something which was confirmed as the 10 member associations met in November.

“This serves as recognition of the leadership of the current FIFA president and the positive transformations within football,” Conmbeol said in a statement.

Caribbean Football Union (25 members) 🌎.

Following a pair of visits to the Caribbean, the CFU announced on Friday that it will endorse Infantino for another term. This is despite Concacaf, the governing body of North America and the Caribbean, being in opposition.

“The CFU emphasizes that it determined its collective position through consultation with its member associations,” the organisation said in a statement. “In this same spirit the CFU continues to call for increased transparency, good governance, and meaningful reform within the football family.”.

Uefa is not fully unified in its opposition of Infantino, with Azerbaijan one of two nations to publicly back the incumbent president.

“The Association of Football Federations of Azerbaijan (AFFA) fully supports Fifa and Fifa President Gianni Infantino,” a statement read after a visit to Hovsan.

Similarly, the association of Latvia has stood in support of Infantino amid criticism from Uefa.

Recent findings suggest that “Gianni Infantino does so many things that it is difficult to list in one minute, but I am grateful for his support around the world, his contribution to the development of football, and, of course, Latvia is always on his side,” said federation president Vadims Lyashenko. “He can count on our support.”.

Benin’s federation looks set to back Infantino in next March’s election.

“I see no reason not to support him,” stated Mathurin de Chacus, president of the Benin federation.

FA president Alexandre Muyenge of Burundi echoed the remarks by his Benin counterpart supporting Infantino.

Sources indicate that he stated: “He is a president who is doing what is necessary to support Africa, particularly the less wealthy countries. His record is good, so it is logical to support him.".

The president of the Comoros Football Federation, Stated Ali Athouman, backed Infantino’s scheme due to the financial benefits to smaller nations.

"Our problem is how to obtain money,” he said. “Right now, we have no sponsors. So how do we compete? The richest nations can train players, have infrastructure and equipment, and it's no coincidence that they then achieve results. Most European countries don't have ​these problems.”.

The Djiboutian Football Federation has similarly welcomed the decision to withdraw the sell-off proposal, with president Souleiman Hassan Waberi saying the climbdown “demonstrates a firm commitment to preserving the unity, solidarity and cohesion that define the football family”.

He said in a statement: “I reaffirm my full support for Fifa President Mr Gianni Infantino and for all initiatives aimed at promoting the sustainable, transparent and inclusive development of football around the world.”.

In a recent development, DR Congo's federation (Fecofa) president Veron Mosengo-Omba, who was only elected in May, spoke out in “full support” of Infantino. The two studied at university in Switzerland together.

Fecofa remarked it had "greatly benefited" from Fifa's programmes, citing investment in development and infrastructure.

Egypt have maintained their endorsement of Infantino, similar to heir North African counterparts.

"The Egyptian Football Association reiterates its full trust in President Gianni Infantino's leadership and its continuous support for any initiatives that benefit Fifa member associations and the future of world football,” a statement read.

Lamin Kaba Bajo told BBC Sport that his federation not just stood by Infantino, but would do "everything within our means" to get him re-elected.

Industry observers note that "That's my personal opinion as president of the federation, and a good number of African memberships also stand on that line. He is here to stay,” he noted.

Fleetwood Haiya, Malawi's football chief, cited the nation’s financial concerns in why he supported Infantino.

He told BBC Sport: "Our government is not able to make sure that they have medical supplies in hospitals and at the same time to look at football. Malawi needs money.".

Ahmed Yahya, the country's representative on the Fifa Council, was one of a number of African football leaders to say he was backing Infantino early on, pledging his support before Caf took its stance.

The location of Infantino’s initial crisis meeting back in the summer, Morocco have stuck by the Swiss-Italian as one of his most loyal allies.

“What has been achieved in recent years through Fifa’s development programmes, particularly in Africa, represents an notable accomplishment that must be preserved, to the benefit of all member associations,” stated the Royal Moroccan Football Federation’s president Fouzi Lekjaa.

Like Mauritania, Hamidou Djibrilla from Niger came out quickly in support of Infantino.

The Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) has largely aligned itself towards a supportive stance for Infantino's leadership, with former NFF president and deputy chairman of Fifa's Men's National Teams Competitions Committee, Amaju Pinnick, backing his initial sell-off strategy.

Namibia Football Association president Robert Shimooshili has backed Infantino and reiterated that his federation stands with Caf.

“If CAF rallies behind Infantino, then we also support the president of Fifa at the moment. We have confidence in him, and we don’t mind what Uefa or AFC or Concacaf say. That is their right and we cannot do anything about it,” he said.

Sudan’s federation joined five other Arab nations - Qatar, Lebanon, Morocco, Egypt and Mauritania - in writing a joint statement backing Infantino.

Recent findings suggest that "Recognising the notable role of Arab football in bringing people together and strengthening co-operation among football associations across the Arab world, we ... express our full support for Mr Gianni Infantino, president of Fifa, and reaffirm our confidence in his leadership and continued commitment to the development of football worldwide," the statement read.

According to recent reports, "We deeply appreciate Mr Infantino’s sustained efforts to advance football globally, expand opportunities across all regions and strengthen the game’s role in bringing people and communities together. We look forward to continuing our close cooperation with him towards a stronger and more prosperous future for world ‌football, expanding opportunities and further enhancing Arab football’s contribution to ​the global game.".

While not an official statement from the federation, South Africa’s Minister of Sports, Arts and Culture of South Africa, Gayton McKenzie, posted on X saying that Infantino had been "very good to African football".

Industry observers note that "Africa should be cautious in joining the public lynching of Infantino,” he warned. “He has been very good to African football. We can debate his ideas but let's not forget who has been a friend to us. Many of those calling for his head want the old status quo back too.".

The Ugandan federation are noted to have echoed the sentiments of Malawi and comoros, with football officials from the federation telling BBC Sport that Fifa investment has transformed their game both on and off the pitch.

The Bhutan Football Federation has published a letter that extends its “sincere appreciation” to Infantino for scrapping the plans, hailing him for demonstrating “true leadership” by “prioritising consensus over commerce”.

“We stand united with Fifa and President Infantino in their ongoing efforts to serve the global football community,” wrote federation president Dasho Ugen Tsechup.

Like others, Kuwait welcomed the decision to halt the aims but Sheikh Ahmed Yusuf Al-Sabah, the president of the Kuwait Football Association, affirmed his support for Infantino.

A statement read: “He concluded by affirming the Kuwait Football Association's confidence in the leadership of Fifa President Gianni Infantino, and its support for efforts aimed at developing the game and enhancing its opportunities for growth in a way that serves all national associations and achieves the shared interests of global football.”.

Lebanon, who granted Infantino citizenship last year, have backed the Swiss-Italian, with FA president Hashim Haidar all but echoing the same sentiments as Kuwait.

According to recent reports, “Haidar reaffirms the Lebanese Football Association’s support for Fifa President Gianni Infantino and his confidence in the decisions he makes in the best interests of global football, as well as in his efforts and initiatives aimed at developing the game,” he noted, while also asserting that Infantino’s proposal “could be re-examined ... in a away that serves the greater good of the sport and preserves its unity”.

The president of the Indonesian FA supported Infantino’s sell-off plan and has now backed him for another term.

Hailing Fifa as a “strategic partner that is truly present” in its football development, Erick Thohir stated: “This is proof of President Infantino’s vision that football development must not be centered on a single region; it must proceed worldwide.”.

The Mongolian Football Federation has likewise put out a statement in support of Infantino.

Qatar was the first football association to publicly back Infantino during his attempts to sell off the World Cup, even though they later welcomed the decision to scrap the proposal.

"While the proposal had merit, we applaud the wisdom behind prioritising unity among member associations. The Qatar Football Association fully supports President Infantino's efforts to continue growing and strengthening the game globally,” a statement read.

Philippines have also backed Infantino and called for co-operation among confederations.

"We stand behind President Gianni Infantino's leadership, and trust that continued dialogue among all confederations and member associations will keep the global game moving forward together,” the Philippines confirmed.

Saudi Arabia, the controversial host of the 2034 World Cup, unsurprisingly came out in support of Infantino in the fallout of the scandal.

"At this time, SAFF supports the continued efforts ​of Fifa President Gianni Infantino and Fifa’s leadership to restore unity across ⁠the football family and continue growing the game for the benefit of all," ​the federation stated in a statement on its website.

Like Qatar, Sri Lanka welcomed the decision to scrap the investment plan and has since reaffirmed its support for Infantino.

It has been revealed that "One of President Infantino's defining leadership qualities has always been his willingness to listen to the views and concerns of Member Associations. This decision is a clear reflection of his inclusive leadership style, built on dialogue, mutual respect, and a genuine commitment to serving the global football community," its statement read.

The UAE Football Association backed Infantino after Fifa withdrew its proposed private investment initiative, with president Sheikh Hamdan bin Mubarak Al Nahyan saying the FA “reaffirmed its confidence” in his leadership.

Argentina became the first member from South America to voice its support for Infantino, on the same day that confederation Conmebol - which had previously only expressed backing of Infantino - expressed concern over Fifa’s procedures.

"Of our highest consideration, on behalf of the Argentine Football Association (AFA), and its Executive Committee, we address you, dear President, and through your worthy intermediary the Fifa board, to express our support for the management carried out during the last 10 years, which had as its main axes the development of football throughout the world and institutional solidity based on a clear governance model, stable and transparent,” a statement read.

The Ecuador federation (FEF) welcomed the proposal’s withdrawal and expressed confidence in Infantino’s leadership.

“We trust that you, and those who are presently leading football, will continue working for the benefit of our sport,” read the statement.

Paraguay also followed suit as Infantino’s Conmebol support base surfaced.

Their federation published a letter of support addressed to Infantino, writing that it "reaffirms its commitment to continue working alongside Fifa”.

Venezuela was another from South America to publicly support Infantino.

“We reiterate our commitment to continue working shoulder to shoulder under your leadership and with the other sister associations to promote the massification and excellence of all modalities of our discipline,” read a statement from the federation.

One of the many island nations to break away from Concacaf is Antigua and Barbuda, with the Caribbean being re-established as an Infantino stronghold.

Industry observers note that “[Infantino’s] transformative policies, from ground-breaking investment in grassroots infrastructure to the historic expansion of World Cup access, have elevated the aspirations of emerging football nations into attainable realities,” the ABFA mentioned in a statement. “By listening with genuine humility and acting with decisive conviction, he has forged a legacy of inclusivity that transcends the sport itself, affirming that every nation, regardless of size, deserves equal voice and fair opportunity on the world stage.”.

Another Caribbean federation to support Infantino’s leadership is the British Virgin Islands.

BVI FA president Avanell Morton noted: “Well, what more can he do? He’s doing a fantastic job already and doing a fantastic job for the entire region. It’s about football and as long as you are about football, then you have the opportunity to make football the priority.”.

Grenada’s federation (GFA) has also broken away from the Concacaf block and reaffirmed its support for Infantino.

“The GFA reaffirms its support for Fifa President Gianni Infantino and expresses its sincere appreciation for his continued support for football development in Grenada and across the Caribbean over his period of service in office and for the years to come,” a statement read.

JFF president Michael Ricketts has similarly reaffirmed his federation’s support in Infantino, breaking away from the Concacaf stance.

“I think Infantino has done so very well for football globally,” he mentioned. “I remember when I got into football as the president, the support from Fifa was medial to say the least.It has been a lot better now and we are just very grateful and we are looking forward to further improvements so that we can impact not just football but the social well-being of every boy and girl who plays the sport.”.

Mexico is the only non-Caribbean Concacaf member to support Infantino, breaking away from the stance taken by its 2026 World Cup co-hosts, the United States and Canada.

The Mexican Football Federation (FMF) stated: "The FMF will neither recognise nor approve any process convened outside of that institutional framework, and it joins the call made... by President Infantino to collectively continue developing football for the benefit of the 211 member associations.".

The Saint Kitts and Nevis Football Association (SKNFA) has welcomed Infantino’s decision to scrap the blueprint, called for respect of Fifa’s institutional processes and backed the president to continue.

It remarked: “The SKNFA concluded by reaffirming its support for Infantino’s leadership and vision, and said it looks forward to supporting him as he completes his current constitutional mandate and continues efforts to advance football development across Fifa’s 211 Member Associations.”.

One of just three Caribbean nations to ever qualify for a World Cup, Trinidad and Tobago president Kieron Edwards says he has no doubts that the TTFA will back Infantino next year.

“We would have given President Infantino our full support and we have not wavered with that. Things do come up, changes, you have to have discussions, you have to have dialogue but the support is there 100 per cent behind the President always,” he said.

With the Oceania Football Confederation yet to take an official stance, the Football Federation of American Samoa to come out on their own and back Infantino, sending a letter to the incumbent president to express “sincere gratitude for your outstanding leadership of the the Fifa family worldwide”.

Latest Caledonia federation president Steeve Laigle has acknowledged Infantino’s “political mistake” but continues to defend the Fifa chief, whose World Cup expansion allowed the tiny Pacific island to reach a World Cup play-off.

Papua New Guinea’s association (PNGFA) was quick to “reaffirm its full support for Fifa president Gianni Infantino” in the aftermath of his botched privatisation bid.

The Solomon Islands also expressed its “continued confidence in his leadership” in regards to Infantino’s presidency.

Tahiti are also noted to have expressed their support before the OFC have taken an official stance.

The Oceania Football Confederation (OFC), with its 11 member associations, stopped short from pulling its support for Infantino in their statement after welcoming the scrapping of the sell-off blueprint, very much staying on the fence as it called for a “review”.

A statement read: "The OFC recognises the progress achieved over the last decade in advancing football development in Oceania under Fifa's leadership and encourages Fifa to use the review as an opportunity to identify and implement any changes that may be necessary.".

Individual members of the confederation have already taken stances, as seen above.

As things stand, The Independent tallies that Infantino has 142 member associations backing him for re-election, while 71 members are outwardly confirmed to be opposing him. This is taking into account the endorsements of confederations, which are being considered as a blanket vote from all members under that governing body unless a member has broken rank.

For example, Jordan’s opposition to Infantino means he is not included in the other 46 AFC member associations supporting Infantino, per the confederation’s endorsement, while the likes of Mexico, Jamaica, Trinidad and Tobago and more are all separate from the other Concacaf members in opposition.

This suggests that Infantino is well on course for re-election. However, each nation has a vote for itself and some could go against their confederation’s stance. Japan’s decision to run a rival candidate signifies Asia is not unanimous with its support of Infantino, with Tashima having at least five other member associations backing him - something he will later reveal. Meanwhile, the Brazilian federation president publicly opposed Infantino’s sell-off prepares and may not be aligned with Conmebol.

Nevertheless, there will need to be a massive swing from within Infantino’s strongholds if the tide is to turn against the Swiss-Italian come next March’s election.

#48126. Industry News: Inside women’s football’s difficult rise in Syria: ‘A joy that everyone in the country needed’

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (2061 w)

Industry News: Inside women’s football’s difficult rise in Syria: ‘A joy that everyone in the country needed’

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2061 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Theguardian

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that A 14-year civil war ravaged the country and ground women’s football to a halt.
  • In December 2024, Syria’s under-18 women’s football team boarded a last-minute bus at midnight from Aqaba, bound for Damascus.
  • Back home, a war that had been largely frozen for four years was suddenly moving at pace.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that A 14-year civil war ravaged the country and ground women’s football to a halt. Today, the first glimmers of hope are beginning to emerge amid difficulty.

In December 2024, Syria’s under-18 women’s football team boarded a last-minute bus at midnight from Aqaba, bound for Damascus. The players had been in Jordan preparing for their final match of the WAFF women’s championship, where a win against Saudi Arabia would have kept their hopes of winning the title alive. Syria pulled out amid fears that the border would close.

Back home, a war that had been largely frozen for four years was suddenly moving at pace. Rebel forces had swept out of the northwest, taking Aleppo and were pushing south towards the capital, 350km away, threatening to topple the now-former president, Bashar al-Assad. Players from the provinces around Damascus made their way home. But those from Hasakah, in the country’s far north-east, spent the next three days stranded at Damascus airport, as airline staff fled and planes sat idle on the tarmac, until a bus was finally able to take them home.

In a recent development, scared, exhausted and running on adrenaline, the team had lived through another episode of disruption; but in truth they had rarely known stability. For Syrian women’s footballers, navigating uncertainty had been part of the game long before the country’s political upheaval reached its latest turning point. “My generation was burned away and completely lost,” said Noor Jumaa, a former national team goalkeeper. “It was like everything that was being built just disappeared.”.

Sources indicate that after 14 years of war, Syria has much to rebuild. Women’s football is among the institutions trying to recover from a conflict that erased an entire generation of players, interrupted the development of the game itself and left its infrastructure struggling. Yet, in recent years, Syria’s youth teams have emerged as one of the country’s more unexpected sporting success stories, winning regional titles and producing players who are beginning to make their mark abroad.

Syria’s women’s national team played their first international match in 2005. By 2011, plans were under way for an 11-a-side women’s league. Then the uprising began, and all plans were abandoned. For the next six years, women’s football in Syria effectively stopped. There were no international fixtures at any level, only occasional futsal tournaments. More than six million people eventually fled Syria, including hundreds involved in the sport, leaving an already small pool of players scattered across the world.

Men’s football, by contrast, continued. The national team played matches abroad after Syria was barred from hosting fixtures in 2011 on security grounds. The Assad regime used its successes to project an image of normality, even welcoming the squad to his palace after their 2012 WAFF Championship victory. Fifa, despite its rules against political interference, stayed silent.

Girls growing up in those years had no women’s team to watch. “I was watching a match of Syria’s men’s national team, and I was really upset. I would say, ‘God, if only they’d make a national team for girls,’” recalled Raneem Abo Lateef, a 21-year-old goalkeeper for Syria. The opportunity came unexpectedly after her family moved houses, and a girl next door told Abo Lateef that a relative was starting a girls’ club. “Girls’ football? Wow,” she remarked. “It was like dreams coming true.”.

Industry observers note that similarly, international teammate Julnar Mustafa spent hours playing with boys in her neighbourhood in Hasakah. Born in 2008, so too young to remember the beginning of the uprising, she filmed herself dribbling and performing tricks on her phone, uploading the videos to Facebook. A regional coach came across them and invited Mustafa to join his team.

But finding an opportunity to play was only part of the challenge. “In our society, especially in the north, in Hasakah, sport is completely off-limits for girls,” Mustafa told the Guardian. “Not football, not anything”.

While a latest generation of girls were finding their way into football, the national team was attempting to return to international competition. In April 2017, Syria entered the Asian Cup qualifiers in Vietnam, assembling a squad after six years without any activity. The federation confirmed tryouts on Facebook, and players were given about a month of preparation. Syria went on to lose every match, including a 14-0 defeat by Myanmar. “Honestly, it was one of the worst teams in Syria’s history,” mentioned Jumaa, who was part of that squad. “We lost by terrifying scores.”.

Maha Al-Katreb, also in the squad at the time, remembers the criticism that followed. Players were ridiculed despite having had little preparation. At the tournament, she saw opponents arrive with larger coaching staffs and younger players training alongside their senior teams. The gap between Syria and their regional competitors was difficult to ignore.

With injuries ending her career early, Al-Katreb fell into coaching by chance and turned towards building a programme that could develop the next generation. She later joined the Syrian Football Association (SFA), taking on administrative and coaching responsibilities.

Sources indicate that A six-team women’s senior league was established in 2019, followed by the development of youth national teams. This year the country held an inaugural edition of its youth league. Al-Katreb developed Syria’s first women’s football strategy, submitted to Fifa, that set out a longer-term blueprint for expanding participation and creating a pathway into the national teams. “You have to start building from the bottom if you want to see results after these 10 years,” Al-Katreb said. “So that we don’t burn one generation after another.”.

In 2022, women accounted for only 1,000 of Syria’s 25,000 registered footballers. The women’s football strategy, seen by the Guardian, aimed to increase female participation by 150% over four years, including through 33 school training centres across 11 provinces, with capacity for 1,650 girls by 2026.

Industry observers note that the government has also outlined prepares to rehabilitate the country’s sporting infrastructure. Rami Alsubea, an adviser at the Ministry of Sport and Youth, mentioned in a statement that 48 sports facilities had been rehabilitated in 2025, with plans to rehabilitate about 150 more and build about 20 new ones by 2028. Restoring infrastructure is in part to meet hosting criteria set by Fifa and the Asian Football Confederation (AFC).

Al-Katreb left the federation more than a year ago. Jumaa is now part of a two-woman team leading its women’s football department, appointed after the arrival of the federation’s current president, Feras al-Teet. Several players have criticized the federation’s leadership and the pace of progress. The Guardian reached out to Al-Teet for comment. He declined.

Among the players who have been vocal about the shortcomings is 26-year-old Rona Aizouk, one of the most experienced members of the current generation. Named after Brazilian footballer Ronaldinho, she made history in 2023 when she became the first Syrian-born woman to sign a professional contract, joining Saudi side Najmat Jeddah. Her performances in Syria had attracted the club’s attention, but securing the move proved difficult. Visa refusals and paperwork complications delayed her arrival until two days before the season began. Her time in Saudi Arabia lasted only a few months, and she was unable to extend her stay.

Sources indicate that “Honestly, I went there not wanting to come back,” noted Aizouk. “There’s no comparison. Everything is better, the treatment, the training, the facilities. It’s just different.

Industry observers note that “The most vital thing is the players’ comfort. Here in Syria, we have to endure psychological pressure and torment. As a player, I have to fight the world just to achieve even a little bit of success.”.

After returning to Damascus to complete her studies, Aizouk promptly received interest from multiple clubs in Jordan, where she now plays. For her, being in situ abroad is about more than personal progression. “I want to be a message that I, who came out of hard circumstances and out of a war, still managed to succeed.”.

It has been revealed that aizouk’s exposure to regional excellence has shown her that Syria is still many years behind. At the forefront is financial restriction that has left the sport bare-boned. International sanctions and banking restrictions imposed on Syria left millions of dollars in development funding from Fifa inaccessible to the SFA, preventing it from fully benefiting from programmes such as Fifa Forward.

It has been revealed that although broad economic sanctions have since been lifted, an estimated $11.5m in funds remains inaccessible to the federation. Both the SFA and Fifa insist they are working to establish a mechanism through which the money can be transferred. For now, the support has been seen in training equipment.

The financial strain is felt directly by players as both the national team and regional league are operated by the SFA. Clubs frequently go months without paying wages, and when payments do arrive, players say they can fall short of the amounts agreed. International call-ups offer little relief: during national team duty, including training camps, players receive a daily allowance of $20, capped at $200 for the length of their stay, regardless of how long it is. Some say the costs of travelling and playing can exceed what they receive.

According to recent reports, several clubs have folded since the domestic league’s launch in 2019, citing financial difficulties and the continued disruption caused by the war and ongoing conflicts. Those that remain often struggle to provide even basic resources.

Recent findings suggest that al-Hilal, now renamed Qamishlo Sport, have become one of the country’s most successful women’s sides, currently reigning as senior and youth league champions. But their achievements have not translated into financial security, according to head coach, Daleel Khalid. “There’s an absence of adequate support from all sides and the parties responsible for Syrian women’s sports, whether in terms of training camps and preparation, or the capabilities and infrastructure needed to develop the game,” he remarked.

The club’s campaign at the 2026 WAFF Women’s Clubs Championship was a massive test. The tournament brought together league champions from six regional competitions. Despite having only a short training camp at home, Al-Hilal reached the final against Saudi champions Al-Nassr. Abo Lateef and Mustafa were among those who represented them, and their performances offered a reminder that Syrian teams can compete with the region’s best, even when their opponents have considerably greater resources.

It has been revealed that there was also individual recognition. Al-Hilal’s Mai Al-Jani was named the tournament’s best player after a series of standout performances, an achievement she was quick to share with those around her. “The award I won is a source of pride for me, for the club and for the players. I see it as a team award,” she noted. “It belongs to the staff, the players, and every Syrian girl living through these difficult circumstances.”.

Born in 2006 in a small village in Homs province, Al-Jani has emerged as one of Syria’s promising attacking talents. She won the league’s Golden Boot in the 2024-25 season and has continued to impress for both club and country. She was also named the best player at the 2023 WAFF under-17 championship, when Syria won their first international title in women’s football. Al-Katreb, who was an assistant coach, saw the victory as evidence of what the country could build with the right support.

Industry observers note that the WAFF under-17 triumph was repeated at the 2026 edition with a completely different squad. “It was joy that everyone in the country needed,” stated Jumaa. “We were completely outnumbered in technical and admin staff, with only nine of us managing everything. Other teams had double the number of staff, with gameplay technology we can’t get our hands on.”.

Recent findings suggest that for Abo Lateef, the greatest risk is allowing another generation of players to lose the chance to compete. The senior women’s national team, for instance, has not played in over two years, with no reason given to players. “We need competition, regardless of the level,” remarked Abo Lateef. “I’m afraid a day will come when I’m made to sit at home, as was the case with the ones before us. A friendly fixture is a good start. Anything.”.

Aizouk’s message to those responsible for the future of the women’s game was more direct. “Save Syrian football,” she mentioned. “Save the generations. Save us.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Harry Maguire and Alexis Mac Allister are among 13 players on the brink of a one-match ban.
  • The first one-match suspensions for yellow card offences in the 2026-27 Premier League season have now been served.
  • Hull City's Matt Crooks and Aston Villa's Matty Cash became the first players to receive a ban for accumulating five yellow cards before gameweek 19.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Harry Maguire and Alexis Mac Allister are among 13 players on the brink of a one-match ban.

The first one-match suspensions for yellow card offences in the 2026-27 Premier League season have now been served.

Hull City's Matt Crooks and Aston Villa's Matty Cash became the first players to receive a ban for accumulating five yellow cards before gameweek 19.

Players receive a one-match suspension if they pick up five or more yellow cards prior to the conclusion of their team's 19th league match of the season.

There are now 13 players sitting on four bookings after 10 rounds of matches, meaning they must avoid another yellow card prior to the halfway point of the season to avoid a ban.

Bournemouth have the most players on the brink of a ban, with three players one yellow card away from suspension.

After that date, the threshold increases to 10 yellow cards. Any player reaching that number before the end of their club's 32nd league match of the season will receive a two-match suspension.

From that point, there are further thresholds at 15 and 20 yellow cards.

According to recent reports, for players reaching 15 cautions, they incur a three-match suspension. Punishments for players reaching 20 yellow cards are determined by a regulatory commission.

Those cut-offs do not reset until the end of the Premier League season.

In the Championship, League One and League Two, there are similar thresholds.

However, with those three divisions having 46 rounds of league matches instead of 38, players have to avoid getting 10 yellow cards before the end of the 37th league match in order to not receive a two-match suspension.

In those divisions, the yellow cards are reset at the end of the league season and do not include matches in the play-offs.

The following players have served a one-match ban and will now receive a two-match ban if they reach ten bookings before game week 32:.

Matt Crooks - Hull City (five yellow cards).

Matty Cash - Aston Villa (five).

If any of the following players receive another Premier League yellow card before the season's halfway point, they will be banned for one match:.

Vitaly Janelt - Brentford (four).

Oli McBurnie - Hull City (four).

Harry Maguire - Manchester United (four).

Pascal Gross - Brighton & Hove Albion (four).

Ethan Ampadu - Leeds United (four).

Oliver Boscagli - Brighton & Hove Albion (four).

Adam Smith - Bournemouth (four).

Marcus Tavernier - Bournemouth (four).

Antonio Silve - Bournemouth (four).

Yeremy Pino - Crystal Palace (four).

Alexis Mac Allister - Liverpool (four).

James McAtee - Nottingham Forest (four).

The following players will miss their club's next set of fixtures:.

Max Dowman - Arsenal (red card suspension).

Jean-Philippe Mateta - Crystal Palace (red card suspension).

Igor Thiago - Brentford (red card suspension).

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that there are two non-negotiables for Chelsea managers.
  • Just as Spurs broke their Stamford Bridge hoodoo a few weeks ago, Leeds secured their first win at Chelsea since 1999 by humiliating the hosts after falling a goal behind.
  • It was 67 long years since Chelsea had last lost at home to Tottenham and Leeds in the same season, and Alonso was left in no doubt about how seriously supporters take that as his team were loudly booed and he was heckled.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that there are two non-negotiables for Chelsea managers. Do not lose at home to Tottenham Hotspur and do not lose at home to Leeds United. But Xabi Alonso has now completed the nightmare double.

Just as Spurs broke their Stamford Bridge hoodoo a few weeks ago, Leeds secured their first win at Chelsea since 1999 by humiliating the hosts after falling a goal behind.

It was 67 long years since Chelsea had last lost at home to Tottenham and Leeds in the same season, and Alonso was left in no doubt about how seriously supporters take that as his team were loudly booed and he was heckled.

Cole Palmer stormed down the tunnel at full time, ignoring the advice of Chelsea’s so-called “cultural architect” Willie Isa to applaud the remaining home fans, and shrugging off the attention of injured striker João Pedro.

Having been left out of the last England squad, Palmer was largely anonymous for Chelsea but he was not alone and Alonso is already facing similar questions to his predecessors about the team’s mentality.

“I felt that probably we are in a fragile moment, mentally,” Alonso said. “When we receive a punch, we didn’t recover that strong, that tough enough and today that was my feeling.

“The fans were disappointed because the expectations from them are high and we feel sorry for them. For sure, it’s not the easiest moment. It’s a fragile moment, but we need to work together and stick together because there is still a long way to go.”.

Alonso is yet to name the same starting XI for successive league games and there appears to be no discernible plan or style of play.

Injuries have contributed to Chelsea’s unremarkable start to the season under Alonso – and Moisés Caicedo was forced off early in the first half – but the problems run deeper than the treatment table.

Industry observers note that alonso’s defence has now conceded 20 goals, which has contributed to Chelsea losing five league games already – more than Manchester United. In between three defeats in their last four league games, Chelsea were also knocked out of the Carabao Cup.

The Spaniard had answered questions about Chelsea’s identity, or lack of it, by saying he wanted his team to be competitive. But they were anything but against a Leeds side who had seven more shots than their hosts and five more on target.

It is hard to fathom how, through all the chopping and changing, Wesley Fofana still starts games for Chelsea in defence. It was his pathetic attempted header, which bounced backwards towards his own goal, that contributed to Noah Okafor’s first goal.

Josh Acheampong also got himself into a mess and Okafor was somehow able to squeeze a shot past goalkeeper Emi Martínez despite having three Chelsea players around him.

Chelsea had taken the lead through striker Emmanuel Emegha, on his first start for the club, but from that moment on they were second best with Leeds pair Ethan Ampadu and Ao Tanaka running the middle of the park.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin had hit the crossbar and failed to find the net with three more presentable opportunities in the first half, but he took his chance from the penalty spot eight minutes after the break.

Morgan Rogers had argued that James Justin’s shot hit him too far up his arm for it to be a penalty, but a VAR check upheld referee Michael Oliver’s decision and Calvert-Lewin kept his cool.

That should have been the moment that shook Chelsea into action and prompted a response but, instead, Alonso’s team fell apart and he was unable to provoke a shift in momentum from the touchline.

Just five minutes after Calvert-Lewin had put Leeds ahead, Okafor effectively sealed the victory by firing the ball into the net after Chelsea had failed to deal with a long throw into their penalty area.

Noah Okafor's brace helps seal Leeds' first Premier League win at Stamford Bridge since 1999! 💥 https://t.co/UAmsJziJmZ.

“I can’t wait to be on the sofa with coffee and cake and also watch this game back because it was a really good game,” Daniel Farke, the Leeds head coach, stated. “I was a bit disappointed even at half-time when it was just a draw, because I think we were the better side from the first to the last.”.

In a recent development, john Terry still works with Chelsea’s academy and it might be worth Alonso getting the former captain to speak to the club’s senior players about how to defend and compete. Whatever has been done on the training pitch so far has not worked.

Recent findings suggest that alonso’s substitutes are yet to register a single goal or assist in the league this season and his changes failed to make any sort of impact here. For the visitors, however, two substitutes combined to score their fourth goal in time added on for stoppages.

Harry Wilson played in Brenden Aaronson and, from a tight angle, he managed to find the back of the net by sending the ball through the legs of Martínez.

The home stands were already half-empty by that point, but some supporters hung around to show their displeasure and Palmer could not contain his anger.

According to recent reports, we know what the history of this game is like and what the fans expect - we know they have wanted a win here for a long time. It’s right we can enjoy this performance.

Frank’s start to life at Palace begins with defeat but an improved display. Coventry are up to 13th with their fourth win of the season.

Another home win for Tottenham, who managed the game well and introduced a fresh star to the Premier League in Williams-Barnett.

Industry observers note that what a day for Leeds. They scored four and it could have been more. For Chelsea, they lost their way when Caicedo went off and without Joao Pedro, they have lost their spark in attack.

Bournemouth make it nine wins in a row in all competitions after doing enough in the first half to get the job done.

Leeds finish the match in style as Aaronson puts the seal on an impressive away day.

It’s all over and Sunderland deservedly leave with a point. Villa will be very disappointed by their display.

What was I saying in the last post?! The home side are on the attack Thomas-Asante pokes a shot at goal and forces Henderson into a save but hits his own player McNeil, who bundles the ball in the net.

Recent findings suggest that can Chelsea stage a late fightback? Will we get a winner between Coventry and Palace?

Needing a goal, Emery makes a bold decision to take off Villa’s top scorer and bring on Madjo.

Despite the two-goal lead and the magnificent debut performance of Luca Williams-Barnett, the home support has remained subdued throughout the afternoon.

At times, the shouts of two children sat just behind the press box feel like by far the loudest noise in the stadium - although that might just be proximity.

Much quieter half at the CBS Arena but Palace are more likely to get a third goal.

This has gone from bad to worse for Chelsea. One supporter near the dug-outs was so angry at Leeds scoring a third goal that he got up and screamed his displeasure at manager Xabi Alonso.

1999 was the last time Leeds won at Chelsea. Today looks like they will get another, as Okafor takes advantage of more poor defending to finish past Martinez.

Villa’s fans are now chanting loudly for substitute John McGinn to be introduced.

They are getting their wish, too, as the Scotland international is coming on with winger Ibrahim Mbaye.

Villa need an injection of energy.

Morgan Rogers and Chelsea are pretty upset about that penalty being awarded to Leeds. They felt the ball struck him too far up his arm to be a penalty. Calvert-Lewin took his spot-kick superbly and it’s gone very, very quiet among the home fans.

Everything Luca Williams-Barnett touches is turning to gold today. He has a goal to his name already, and adds an assist just six minutes into the second half.

From almost the halfway line, he drove forward, weaving his way expertly into the box before picking out Dominic Solanke in the middle of the box, who tapped the ball into the back of the net.

However, the atmosphere is still a touch subdued, despite James Maddison urging the crowd to make themselves heard almost immediately after the goal, the noise drops to almost a murmur.

Sources indicate that rogers blocks Bogle’s drive with his arm and Michael Oliver gives a penalty to Leeds. After a long check, VAR confirms it.

Calvert-Lewin steps up and sends Martinez the wrong way. The away team deserves this. They have been the better side. That is Calvert-Lewin’s 100th club career goal.

Williams-Barnet gets one-on-one with Furlong and gets past him with ease before firing a cross for Solanke to finish.

The whistle blows for the second half around the grounds. What will the second 45 minutes have for us?

A real lack of quality here from both teams, and Sunderland deserve credit for weathering the early pressure.

Villa appear short of creativity and have managed only one shot on target in the first-half.

Sunderland have defended resolutely and caused Villa’s back-four some problems in the rare moments they have attacked.

Unai Emery marched into the dressing room after the half-time whistle and has much to ponder.

Some boos from the Chelsea fans at half-time. Calvert-Lewin could have had a hat-trick in that first half, sending one header against the bar, two too close to Martinez and flicking a shot just wide. Leeds also had a goal ruled out for offside.

Chelsea just stopped playing after taking the lead.

Sources indicate that that half was all about Luca Williams-Barnett. The 18-year-old scored in his first start, and had two opportunities to add to his tally just before the break. He had a header tipped over the bar by Christian Walton and a chance from close range stopped on the line. The future looks bright, as they say.

However, Tottenham faded after a strong opening 15 minutes, and Ipswich were able to break up play and get forward more, exploiting the home side’s lack of a defensive midfielder, and that will be something for Roberto De Zerbi to address in the break.

Sources indicate that we have whistles around the ground. That was breathless stuff.

The visitors will feel they should be in front at the break. First, Muharemovic thinks he has scored when he head in a cross from Justin but he was offside.

Sources indicate that then Ampadu’s long throw finds Calvert-Lewin in space and his shot is saved by Martinez. Should have done better there.

Bournemouth finish the half in style. Kluivert gets the second when he taps in a cross from Tavernier.

Palace hit back again. Pino clips a cross to Larsen at the far post and he heads past Rushworth coolly.

Courtesy of Opta: Aged 18 years and 51 days, Luca Williams-Barnett is Tottenham Hotspur’s youngest Premier League goalscorer since Gareth Bale against Fulham in September 2007 (18y 47d).

According to recent reports, villa are in desperate need of a spark and one has to wonder when John McGinn will be introduced. McGinn is on the bench today and the home team are crying out for some inspiration.

Villa did start brilliantly, yet the game has now petered out into a mess of misplaced passes and poor decision-making.

Still no clean sheet for Emi Martinez. But Noah Okafor’s goal wasn’t his fault – he was let down by some bad defending from Wesley Fofana and Josh Acheampong.

Martinez did start Chelsea’s 2-0 victory over Everton, but he didn’t last the full game as he had to be replaced because of injury.

A touch of Hollywood royalty in attendance at Tottenham on this cold November afternoon with Sir Kenneth Branagh and Ryan Reynolds in attendance.

Reynolds is a co-owner of Wrexham, who are at the moment playing in the Championship at Lincoln City, but he has chosen to watch football in north London instead.

Industry observers note that sakamoto puts Palace back in front with a brilliant finish. Rudoni gets away from Khalaili and crosses to the Japan international. Sakamoto brings it down nicely then rifles a shot into the top corner.

That lead did not last long for Chelsea. The away side hit back within three minutes as Okafor shoots through the legs of Colwill and into the net.

In a recent development, another full debutant and another goal. This time at Stamford Bridge as Emegha latches onto a ball from Rogers and blasts an unstoppable shot from distance.

Emegha had to wait a while to make his first start for Chelsea, but he’s marked it with a really well taken goal. Leeds will be disappointed with the time and space he and Morgan Rogers, who provided the assist, were given, but it was a good finish.

Caicedo just can’t get going this season. That back injury that forced him off the pitch for a minute earlier has now resulted in him having to be replaced by Jordan Henderson. That’s a real blow to Alonso and Chelsea.

Villa were completely dominant in the opening ten minutes but Sunderland have now managed to subdue the home team.

It has been revealed that johan Manzambi and Nicolas Jackson are both impressing for the home team. Villa do appear a little vulnerable in defence when Sunderland do break forward.

Today will be a day that 18-year-old Luca Williams-Barnett will not forget in a hurry, he has been energetic since the start and marked his maiden Premier League start with an early goal.

The actual goal might have been a tap-in, but it has injected life into the crowd who had otherwise been largely subdued from the start.

Confusion on the touchline for Chelsea. Caicedo was down after hurting his back. Alonso tried to stop his phyisos going straight on to the pitch, but referee Michael Oliver called them on. That meant Caicedo had to spend a minute off the pitch under the latest rules.

According to recent reports, remember this moment because on his first senior start Williams-Barnet has made it a special one with goal. It was scrappy but he will not care. The Tottenham fans have been talking about his young fan for a long time.

Equaliser for Palace and Frank. Very good response from his players as Larsen flicks the ball to Pino and the Spain international fires into the net.

No shots on target from either side but it is already shaping up to be attack vs defence. Villa are dominating the goal and looking threatening.

Awoniyi is through one-on-one with Henderson, goes around the keeper but Disasi does brilliantly to recover and make the block.

Worst possible start for Frank and Palace as Awoniyi gets his second goal of the season with a cool finish.

A video of De Zerbi saying “let’s go” in a manner that might be more at home in American Football is shown before the teams come out onto the pitch.

The atmosphere feels a bit subdued so far, but it is an important match for Tottenham.

We are underway around the grounds!

This is probably the kiss of death from me, but I’m really looking forward to watching Tarik Muharemovic today. The defender has impressed me every time I’ve watched Leeds on television this season and looks to be one of the signings of the summer. Dare I say it, but Chelsea could have done worse than sign him given their troubles at the back. Emi Martinez is back in goal for the home side. He’s yet to keep a clean sheet since signing from Aston Villa.

Thomas Frank declared “it’s good to be back in the circus” of football management ahead of his first match as Crystal Palace boss.

The 53-year-old Dane admitted he could have easily spent a few more months sipping wine, “eating too well” and collecting passport stamps, but something resonated when he asked his wife why he was tempted to seek out a latest job and she told him, “(It’s) because you can’t help yourself”.

Frank hinted that there was more behind the story to his disappointing spell at Tottenham he might one day reveal, but for now he has a team to rescue from a relegation fight, beginning with today’s trip to Coventry.

If you don’t learn from any of your jobs, I don’t think you reflect, I don’t think you improve, and I don’t think you get better.

Of course there’s a lot of things I have been reflecting over. The details, that will be for another time, but I can say I’ve learned, definitely.

I was very aware I didn’t want to do anything in the summer. I put a statement out there, I needed more time. I can actually, honestly say I would have been fine if it was three, four, five, six, seven months more, because it’s good to be back in the circus, but it’s also unbelievably good not to be in, especially if you enjoy life, which I do.

I was spending time with family and friends and doing all that, but I think the club, the way Palace is, how well Steve Parish especially spoke about the club and ideas, Matt Hobbs and Iain Moody and these guys, too, helped convince me it was a good idea.

Construction news: work on the North Stand behind one of the Villa Park goals continues to progress.

There are clear structural changes since Villa’s last home game and a mural of fans makes it more appealing to look at.

This stand is scheduled to be ready for next season and will increase Villa’s capacity to over 50,000.

Tottenham’s impressive run of form came to a crashing halt with a 1-0 defeat to Leeds just before the international break, but manager Roberto De Zerbi will be hoping for a fresh start - even if he will not be pitchside after picking up a second yellow card of the season.

De Zerbi made six changes from the aforementioned defeat to Leeds, including a first start for teenager Luca Williams-Barnett, a player who has come through the club’s academy.

There is no place in the squad for Sandro Tonali or Tosin Adarabioyo, but James Maddison will start for the first time since the 2-0 defeat to Chelsea in October.

Aston Villa 2.0 was always likely to be a slow-burner, and it is proving exactly that for Unai Emery.

His team has impressed and underwhelmed in equal measure so far this season but this is an opportunity to hoist themselves up the table.

A clean sheet would be a good starting point, as they have not secured a shutout in front of their own fans in the league since March.

There is no Alejandro Garnacho or Tammy Abraham in the matchday squad today.

Good afternoon and welcome to coverage from the Premier League as domestic football returns after an international break.

We have five matches to bring you, including Chelsea vs Leeds, Aston Villa vs Sunderland and Tottenham vs Ipswich.

Xabi Alonso said his Chelsea side needs to learn to deal with the absence of Joao Pedro as the Blues struggle for goals in the absence of their injured striker.

The Brazilian has not played since the 2-0 win over Everton on October 17 and will be unavailable again today.

Without a focal point in the number nine position, Chelsea’s goal output has been dramatically reduced and they have dropped to fifth and having suffered two defeats in their last three games.

Sources indicate that “(We need) the whole team for that,” noted Alonso. “It’s not just the strikers that can score. We can score from set-pieces, from defenders, from midfielders.

In a recent development, “It’s teamwork. For sure Joao is an key player but we need to deal with this time without him. So far we have tried different options and we need to keep trying.

“We need to deal with it. It’s not that I’m going to look for one explanation. I think that there are more explanations for one defeat than missing just one player.”.

Tottenham will not have their manager, Roberto De Zerbi, on the touchline after receiving three yellow cards this season.

Gary O’Neil is targeting a “special” result at Tottenham, but promised Ipswich will not make any drastic changes after a four-match winless run.

Ipswich lost 2-1 at home to Bournemouth before the two-week break, which followed draws with Hull and Nottingham Forest along with a narrow defeat at Manchester City, but O’Neil is happy with his newly introduced-look group.

“There won’t be any drastic changes. The odd personnel change, (but) I don’t think it’s going to be a significant shift for us,” O’Neil told a press conference.

In a recent development, “It’s a very well-balanced squad. There’s going to be no massive uplifts or downgrades when we have to change players within this group.”.

Aston Villa will have Johan Manzambi available for the visit of Sunderland.

The midfielder did not feature for Switzerland during the recent international break because of a calf injury but he has trained with the rest of the squad and can feature today.

Villa can also call on right-back Aaron Wan-Bissaka after a muscle injury ruled him out for six matches. His return is timely as Matty Cash is unavailable.

Cash was suspended for Villa’s 4-4 draw with Manchester United before the international break but suffered a concussion while away with Poland.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The 2026 National Women's Soccer League (NWSL) Championship final is upon us, with Washington Spirit and Kansas City Current set to battle it out for the title on November 21.
  • Washington booked their third consecutive final appearance with a victory over Utah Royals in the semi-finals, while Kansas City Current overcame reigning champions Gotham FC to move one step closer to lifting the trophy.
